To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

exposure to work organization, physical, and psychosocial factors is associated with shoulder pain in workers, but the effects of work organization factors are mediated by physical and psychosociological risk factors.

exposure to factors related with work organization has a direct effect on physical and psycho-social constraints, psychological demand is the only psycho-social constraint which increases perceived stress, and shoulder-pain is influenced directly by physical constraints for both men and women, and by stress for men.

work pace, application and control of quality standards, and work schedule were associated with physical risk factors, perceived psychological demand was the only factor associated with stress, and shoulder disorders were directly related to physical risk factors for men and women and to stress for men.

the relationship between work organization (i.e., work pace, quality standards), physical and psychosociological risk factors, and perceived stress.
the development of a model of risk factors for shoulder pain, which can be used in prevention.
the study of risk factors for shoulder pain in a French working population.
